location.mountain: Li Shan (one of Taiwan's highest tea zones)

description.short: The highest and most prestigious oolong in Taiwan — exceptionally sweet, ethereal, with persistent alpine floral fragrance
description.overview: Cultivated at some of the highest elevations of any tea gardens in the world, where slow leaf growth yields extreme concentrations of natural sugars and aromatic compounds.
description.leaf: Large, tightly rolled light jade pearls
description.aroma: Sublime mountain floral bouquet, crisp cool air nuance
description.taste: Remarkably smooth, delicate, honey-sweet, free of bitterness, with silky mouthfeel
description.aftertaste: Exceptionally persistent, clean, sweet and cooling
description.processing: Careful high-altitude manual harvest → withering → gentle tossing → kill-green → ball rolling → low-temperature drying

history.origin: Pioneering farmers began planting tea on Li Shan in the 1980s, testing whether extreme alpine altitudes formerly deemed unviable could sustain Camellia sinensis.
history.development: The triumph of those early Li Shan plots demonstrated that extreme elevations above 2,000 meters produced a tea of unmatched sweetness and aromatic purity.
history.modern: Today Li Shan is Taiwan's most prestigious and expensive tea terroir, coveted by connoisseurs and frequently gifted as a luxury emblem in business and diplomacy.
interestingFacts: Li Shan tea gardens are among the highest commercial tea plantations on Earth, rivaled only by high-altitude plots in Darjeeling and Yunnan.
Due to steep terrain and extreme cold, harvests are strictly limited in volume and command premium pricing across international markets.
